name: Muztar
dates: dates not given in the source
bio: The book says Muztar was born and educated at Lucknow, that his ancestors occupied an honourable rank at Delhi, and that he was a pupil of Mushafi. It gives no dates.

The one piece given here is drawn from Hindustani Lyrics (London: The Sufi Publishing Society, 1919), in the English verse of Inayat Khan and Jessie Duncan Westbrook. It is a free rendering, not a literal translation, and the original Urdu poem is untitled; it is named here by its first line.

poems.title: Where has my childhood gone, where are its placid years?
poems.author: Muztar
poems.translator: trans. Inayat Khan and Jessie Duncan Westbrook (1919)
poems.text:
Where has my childhood gone, where are its placid years?
For cruel youth hath brought passion and bitter tears.

To the Creator now I from the dust complain--
Beauty, the thing he made, brings with it only pain.

Long I desired and dreamed, waiting with eager breath,
But ere she came to me, Fate sent the sleep of Death.

To God as servitor I my devotion gave,
Now Love hath taken me, bound me to be his slave.

I, Muztar, die with grief, yearning unsatisfied,
Still hangs the purdah's fold I cannot draw aside,
Nor lift the needless veil woven of shame and pride.
